Research / High-energy astrophysics

Accreting neutron stars
and X-ray pulsars

I study broadband X-ray spectra, pulse profiles and spin evolution to investigate accretion processes in neutron star X-ray binaries.

Doctoral research · IIST · July 2024 — Present

Current focus

Doctoral research

Spectro-temporal studies of accreting neutron star X-ray binaries and X-ray pulsars.

01

Accretion & outbursts

Broadband X-ray observations of changes in accretion flows during outbursts.

02

Spectra & magnetic fields

X-ray continuum modelling and cyclotron resonance features in magnetised accretion flows.

03

Pulsations & spin evolution

Pulse-profile variations and spin-frequency changes associated with accretion.

About the background illustration

A conceptual Be-star / neutron-star binary: the eccentric orbit solves Kepler’s equation, and disk rotation scales as r−3/2. Enhanced gas capture near periastron is illustrative. Sizes, time scales, brightness and gas paths are not a fitted physical model. The animation is decorative; no measured data are shown.

Scientific context: NASA NICER on Be/X-ray binaries and magnetically channelled accretion.
